title: Quectel SH602FA and SE505FE smart modules bring Android 16 to 4G LTE and 5G IoT devices
summary: Quectel has just introduced the SH602FA 4G LTE Cat 4 and SE505FE 5G Sub-6 GHz Android 16-smart IoT modules. Both integrate octa-core MediaTek processors, cellular connectivity, wireless interfaces, and multimedia functions for devices such as smart displays, point-of-sale terminals, industrial handhelds, and robots. The high-performance 4G LTE SH602FA module is built around the MediaTek MT8786 Cortex-A75/A55 processor, while the entry-level 5G SE505FE module is powered by a MediaTek MT8863T Cortex-A76/A55 SoC. Both modules are available in multiple regional variants, as well as a Wi-Fi/Bluetooth-only -WF variant. Quectel SH602FA and SE505FE specifications: From the specifications, the SE505FE is the higher-performance option, with 2 Cortex-A76 cores at up to 2.4 GHz, 5G Sub-6 GHz connectivity with up to 3.27 Gbps downlink and 4 4 DL MIMO, plus support for displays up to 120 Hz and cameras up to 32 MP. title: KAGA FEI ES4L15MA1 is a ridiculously small, ready-to-use BLE 6.0 module based on Nordic nRF54L15 SoC
summary: Japanese company KAGA FEI has introduced another incredibly small ES4L15MA1 Bluetooth LE 6.0 module based on Nordic Semiconductor s nRF54L15 ultra-low-power Cortex-M33 wireless MCU. Launched alongside the larger EC4L15MA1 module, the ES4L15MA1 module appears to be based on the same hardware as the ES4L15BA1 world s smallest module unveiled in 2024 with an 8.55 x 3.25 x 1.00 mm form factor. title: StarFive Dubhe-100 A 64-bit, RVA23-compliant RISC-V core for high-performance applications

title: Pine64 hits pause on Linux devices due to RAM and eMMC shortage/high prices
summary: While some companies keep increasing prices, the Pine64 community has now announced they don t intend to manufacture Linux devices due to the current RAM and eMMC flash shortage and related high prices. Pine64 started with the launch of the Pine A64 development board in 2015, and since then they have launched more Arm and RISC-V Linux SBCs, Linux smartphones, and Linux tablets and e-Readers. We used to get several announcements per year, but this year so far, we only covered one: the Pine64 PineVoice. But it s not a Linux device, and instead, a smart speaker based on a BL602 RISC-V microcontroller. Here s the full (unedited) announcement published on Telegram, which you should also find on other Pine64 channels: Hi everyone! Just a quick reminder that due to the current DRAM/eMMC shortage, there isn t any plans to continue producing more Linux devices in the near future. title: PwrBlock 323 A USB-C PD programmable power supply for automated test fixtures (Crowdfunding)
summary: Finland-based Everypin has introduced the PwrBlock 323, a programmable USB-C PD power supply designed specifically for automated test fixtures. It can provide 1 to 32V at up to 3A, with up to 92W output from a 100W USB-C PD source, and supports software-controlled power switching, voltage and current measurement, and power cycling for a device under test (DUT). The company highlights that the PwrBlock 323 can be mounted inside a test jig or stand using its mounting points and pin headers to control and power the DUT directly as part of the automated test sequence.
